name: Software & SaaS
one_liner: Companies selling software as recurring subscriptions, where near-zero marginal cost and high retention reward scale and punish churn.
how_it_makes_money: Most revenue comes from recurring subscriptions priced per seat, per usage unit, or by tier, often sold on annual or multi-year contracts. Add-ons include professional services, implementation, premium support, and increasingly consumption-based or AI-feature pricing.
revenue_formula: Next-year ARR = starting ARR × net revenue retention + new-logo ARR
ACV = seats × price per seat (or usage units × unit price)
cost_structure: R&D: engineering salaries, often the largest single bucket for younger companies
Sales & marketing: frequently the biggest spend at growth-stage firms, driving customer acquisition
Cost of revenue: cloud hosting, support, and services delivery; gross margins are typically ~70-80%+
G&A: finance, legal, HR; shrinks as a share of revenue with scale
Stock-based compensation: large non-cash expense that shareholders scrutinize
margins: Gross margins are high (roughly 70-85%), but operating margins range from deeply negative for growth-stage firms to ~25-40%+ for mature leaders. The spread is driven by go-to-market efficiency, retention, and how much growth is being bought with S&M spend.

key_metrics.name: Annual recurring revenue (ARR)
key_metrics.what: Annualized value of subscription contracts; the headline measure of scale and growth.

key_metrics.name: Net revenue retention (NRR)
key_metrics.what: Revenue kept from an existing customer cohort after expansion, downgrades, and churn; above ~100% means the base grows on its own.

key_metrics.name: Gross churn
key_metrics.what: Share of revenue or customers lost in a period; the leak that growth must outrun.

key_metrics.name: CAC payback
key_metrics.what: Months of gross profit needed to recover the cost of acquiring a customer; a test of go-to-market efficiency.

key_metrics.name: LTV/CAC
key_metrics.what: Lifetime gross profit of a customer divided by acquisition cost; roughly 3x is a common rule of thumb.

key_metrics.name: Rule of 40
key_metrics.what: Revenue growth rate plus profit (or FCF) margin; balances growth against profitability for valuation.

key_metrics.name: Gross margin
key_metrics.what: Share of revenue left after hosting and support; signals how software-like the business really is.

trends: Generative AI features and agents being bundled into products, raising questions about whether seat-based pricing survives
Shift toward usage- and outcome-based pricing alongside or instead of per-seat licenses
Investor focus moved from growth-at-all-costs to efficient growth and free cash flow
Vendor consolidation as customers cut overlapping tools and push for platform suites
Active private-equity take-privates and roll-ups of mature software companies
Rising inference costs pressuring gross margins for AI-heavy products
